newsitem.title: THAILAND: Former Thai prime minister Seni Pramoj dead at 92.
newsitem.headline: Former Thai prime minister Seni Pramoj dead at 92.

text.p: Seni Pramoj, who served as Thailand's prime minister three times after World War Two, died on Monday. He was 92.
A government spokeswoman said Seni died early in the morning. Local television and radio reports said the former premier died of heart and kidney failure.
Seni, who was ousted from his third and final tenure as prime minister for the Democrat Party after a coup in October 1976, was a national figure for more than three decades.
He served as prime minister of two coalition governments in the mid-1970s, straddling a year-long premiership by his younger brother Kukrit.
Born on May 26, 1905 into a junior branch of the royal family, Seni was educated in Britain and practised law before heading to the United States as Thai ambassador in 1940.
After Japan invaded Thailand in 1941 Seni disassociated himself from the government in Bangkok and organised the anti-Japanese "Free Thai" underground movement.
When occupied Thailand declared war on the United States Seni refused to hand the declaration to the U.S. State Department. As a result, the United States did not declare war on Thailand.
At the end of the war Seni was rushed back to Bangkok to become prime minister, a post he held for only four months.
After a brief stint as minister of justice, Seni returned to the legal profession.

One of his best-known cases occurred in 1961. Seni headed a panel of lawyers to the International Court of Justice in the Hague to challenge a claim by then-Prince Norodom Sihanouk that Thailand had no rights to Phra Viharn, a mountain temple on the border of the two countries. Seni lost the case.
During his time as a lawyer, Seni retained his association with the Democrat Party and eventually became its leader in 1968. He re-entered parliament in 1969.
Seni's second stint as prime minister lasted only a week and he was succeeded by brother in February 1975.
He took over the helm again in April 1976 after Kukrit failed to win a seat in the 1976 election.
